title: How UPI Moves Money in Seconds

segments.say: You buy a cup of tea, scan a code, type your PIN, and the money moves before the tea cools. What just happened?

anim.title: Behind the scan
items: Your bank checks your PIN and debits you
The tea seller's bank credits them

segments.say: Your app sends the request to NPCI, the body that runs UPI. NPCI routes it to your bank, which checks your PIN and takes the money. Then it tells the seller's bank to pay.

anim.title: What makes UPI different
items: One ID instead of an account number

segments.say: Three ideas make it work. A simple ID instead of account numbers. Any app talks to any bank. And it runs round the clock, in real time.

items.text: More than 100 billion payments in a year

segments.say: UPI launched in twenty sixteen. By twenty twenty-four, Indians were making well over a hundred billion UPI payments a year.

left.title: NPCI
items: Set up by RBI and banks

segments.say: NPCI was set up under the RBI's guidance by banks. It doesn't hold your money; banks do. It is the road the money travels on.

anim.title: Beyond India
items: UPI links with other countries' systems
Indians abroad can pay with it in several countries

segments.say: UPI is now linked with payment systems in several other countries, so it is part of India's foreign policy too.
For GS Three: UPI is public digital infrastructure. Interoperable, real-time and cheap, it pulled millions into digital payments.

sources: NPCI, UPI product overview: launched in 2016; instant real-time payment system; interoperable across banks and apps; Virtual Payment Address
NPCI UPI product statistics: annual transactions exceeded 100 billion in calendar 2024 (about 172 billion)
NPCI and RBI: NPCI is an umbrella organisation for retail payments set up under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, as an initiative of RBI and the Indian Banks' Association
NPCI International / PIB releases: UPI linkages with other countries (e.g. Singapore PayNow, 2023)

quiz.why: The National Payments Corporation of India runs UPI.

options: Any app can pay any bank
Only one bank can use it
quiz.why: Any app, any bank: that's interoperability.

reviewNote: Facts were read against NPCI's UPI pages and statistics and PIB releases on international links. No app or bank logos shown. Moving facts: transaction counts grow every month; 'over a hundred billion a year' stays true.
